chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs Tamattu' during the months of Hajj, then stays in Makkah until the Hajj of the following year arrives, upon him is a sheep.'
And the one who performs Tamattu' in other than the months of Hajj, then resides (as a neighbor/sojourner) until the Hajj arrives, there is no blood (sacrifice) upon him.
Rather, it is an individual Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad).
And the sacrifice (Udhiyah/Qurbani) is upon the people of the cities (who reside there).

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and the first ten days of Muharram)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْأَمْصَارِ: People of the cities (residents of Mecca or other major cities)
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The sacrifice (Udhiyah, specifically the Eid al-Adha sacrifice)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performs Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Individual Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad, where Umrah and Hajj are separate)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the sacrificial animal for those performing Tamattu' Hajj versus individual Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the Hajj sacrifice (dam al-hajj) and the Eid al-Adha sacrifice (udhiyah), noting that the latter is primarily obligatory for Ahl al-AmSar (residents of cities). It establishes that a Mu'tamir performing Tamattu' who stays in Mecca until the following year incurs a sheep sacrifice, whereas those who sojourn or perform Hajj outside the specific months are exempt, highlighting the juristic nuance between temporary residency and permanent habitation in Islamic law.
